## Rule

**DECODED 2026-06-08 from the generator (`external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_a8c38be5.py`;
task264 = ARC `a8c38be5`, the 264th sorted ARC-AGI-train UUID).**

The input scatters **9 non-overlapping 3×3 sprites** at random positions on a
black field (grid 14–16 per side; sprites non-overlapping with **spacing ≥1**).
Each sprite is a solid 3×3 of gray(5) overpainted with a **FIXED per-index
colored pattern** — the 8 compass arrows + an empty center:

```
idx0 TL: XX.   idx1 TM: XXX   idx2 TR: .XX
         X..            .X.            ..X
         ...            ...            ...
idx3 ML: X..   idx4 MM:(none) idx5 MR: ..X
         XX.                           .XX
         X..                           ..X
idx6 BL: ...   idx7 BM: ...   idx8 BR: ...
         X..            .X.            ..X
         XX.            XXX            .XX
```

The output is **always 9×9**, gray(5) background, = the 3×3 arrangement of those
sprites: block `(idx//3, idx%3)` is painted with `colors[idx]` in pattern `idx`.
Colors come from `random_color(exclude=[gray])` → **always in {1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9}**
(never 0 or 5). The pattern of each sprite is fixed by its index, so **only the 8
colors vary between instances** — the entire transform = read the 8 colors (one
per directional pattern) and drop them into the fixed template. Provably-exact
detection: a 3×3 window matches sprite-`idx` iff all 9 cells are non-black
(solidity) AND its colored cells form pattern `idx`.

Note: the prior "unknown — inherently hard / 74 Mul + 24 Slice template-matching"
description was of an OLD live graph; the rule was never actually decoded until
the 2026-06-08 siege rewrite below.

### Floor proof (338-standard) — the requested <1500 is PROVABLY unreachable
The output is only 8 colours in a fixed template; the residual cost is the
arbitrary-position spatial scan. Two charged tensors remain forced:
- **`sig32` F32 [1,1,14,14] = 784** — one stride-1 detector channel; F32 and 14×14
  are forced by the F32 input, 16×16 top-left range, and odd-position sprites.
- **`oh_b` BOOL [1,9,9,9] = 729** — the small answer one-hot; #81 Pad-last beats a
  full 30×30 value canvas or direction-keyed ConvTranspose here.
**784 + 729 = 1,513 > 1500**, so <1500 remains unreachable. The remaining
~716 B is MaxPool/TopK/routing/output plumbing plus params.
**2,229 is therefore ~75% of the way from the previous "irreducible 34,606" to the hard 1,513
floor, and within ~716 B of the information-plus-scan limit.**

## Don't-do log

- Do NOT stage 4×4 pre-TopK pooling (`siege_v13`, cost 2,341). It is correct
  for ARC-GEN random draws under `common.overlaps(..., spacing=1)`, but a fixed
  official pair violates that placement invariant: two sprites share one 4×4
  detector block, so MaxPool drops one and visible is **264/265**. Use the
  official-safe 3×3 pooling family (`siege_v14+`; current v22 still uses it)
  instead.
- Do NOT use a direction signature that assigns code 0 to a colored sprite while
  still extracting all 9 sprites. TopK then extracts the all-gray center sprite
  too; it has code 0 and must remain a routed-nowhere dummy. `siege_v16/v17`
  used an 8-bin signature with one colored direction at 0 and failed visible
  (~54–55%). The safe exception is v22: the detector ranks only the 8 colored
  sprites above the center, so `TopK(k=8)` never carries the center dummy.
- Do NOT remove the Round node before Cast(F16→UINT8) in the color chain
  (`v21` probe, 2026-06-20). ORT's Mul kernel has sub-ulp precision:
  `Mul(0.28125_f16, 21.328125_f16)` computes 5.999... internally rather than
  exactly 6.0. Without Round, `Cast(5.999_f16, UINT8) = 5` (truncation), giving
  wrong colors. Round(5.999) = 6.0 → Cast = 6 (correct). Round is NECESSARY.
  `v21` produced score 2277 locally but gave 0/265 visible (**abandon**).
- Do NOT change bd9_i INT32 [9] to a narrower dtype (UINT8, INT8, INT16).
  ORT ScatterElements rejects any non-INT32/INT64 index tensor with "Type Error:
  Type 'tensor(uint8)' of input parameter (indices) of operator (ScatterElements)
  is invalid." Only INT32 and INT64 are accepted (2026-06-20 physical test).
- Do NOT remove Min(bd9, clip_hi) / bd9_c to save the 18B intermediate + 1 param.
  The scorer's profiler run uses a dummy all-black input; this produces topv=−126 →
  bd9=126. Without Min, ScatterElements receives index 126 on bins0[9] → ORT
  crashes with "indices element out of data bounds, idx=126". Min IS necessary.
  (2026-06-20; verified the dummy-run path explicitly.)
- Old pre-siege byte-trims (`v2` scalar ones, omitted Slice steps, sparse
  template/ConstantOfShape ideas, and `starts` inlining) are archived in
  `_archive/task264_history.md`; they do not touch the current Siege graph.
- **task264 has a Kaggle-public-negative history** for older cost-only shrinks
  that locally looked byte-equal. Current Siege/v22 candidates meet the higher
  safety bar because they are generator-derived, truth **200000/200000**, and
  A/B byte-equal to the current live graph on **200265/200265**.
